record.paper_title: Space and Time Complexity of Exact Algorithms: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: For BISECTION, where the input is an n-vertex graph G = (V, E) and the task is to find a subset X of V with |X| = n/2 minimizing the number of edges between X and V - X, can one improve on the O*(2^(omega n/3))-time approach, where omega is the matrix multiplication exponent and O* suppresses polynomial factors?

evidence.quote: The approach of Williamson yields an O*(2omega n/3) time algorithm for BISECTION. Can you do better?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E) be an undirected graph on n vertices, where n is even. A bisection of G is a subset X ⊆ V with |X| = n/2; its cut size is the number of edges of G with exactly one endpoint in X. The BISECTION problem asks for a bisection X minimizing this cut size. Let ω denote the exponent of square matrix multiplication, i.e., the infimum of real numbers t such that two n × n matrices can be multiplied in O(n^t) arithmetic operations, and let O*(·) suppress factors polynomial in n.

There is a known exact algorithm solving BISECTION in time O*(2^(ωn/3)). Design an exact algorithm for BISECTION running in time O*(c^n) for some constant c < 2^(ω/3), or prove that no such improvement is possible.
artifact.category_tag: Exact exponential algorithms for graph partitioning
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not surface a published exact algorithm for BISECTION on general graphs that improves on the O*(2^(ωn/3)) bound. Related work focuses on FPT algorithms parameterized by cut size (e.g., 2^O(k^3) n^3 log^3 n by Cygan et al.) and on practical branch-and-bound combinatorial algorithms, neither of which directly addresses the worst-case exponential exponent in n. The status appears to remain unresolved based on available sources.

status_evidence.title: Minimum Bisection Is Fixed-Parameter Tractable
status_evidence.snippet: FPT algorithm for Minimum Bisection with running time 2^O(k^3) n^3 log^3 n, parameterized by the cut size k.
status_evidence.claim: Known improvements are parameterized by cut size, not in n; does not improve worst-case O*(2^(ωn/3)).

status_evidence.title: An Exact Combinatorial Algorithm for Minimum Graph Bisection
status_evidence.snippet: Branch-and-bound exact combinatorial algorithm for minimum graph bisection; practical but without improved worst-case exponential bound.
status_evidence.claim: No improved worst-case exponential running time over O*(2^(ωn/3)) is claimed.
